role: Jamaat politician and convicted war-crimes defendant
contribution: Delwar Hossain Sayeedi was a Jamaat-e-Islami politician whose International Crimes Tribunal case became a major focus of the 2013 Shahbag mobilization and its counter-mobilization.
context: The tribunal convicted him in 2013 over 1971-related crimes and sentenced him to death; the Supreme Court later commuted the sentence to imprisonment. His case was accompanied by intense political mobilization and criticism of the tribunal's fairness.
impact: Sayeedi's case shaped Bangladesh's debate over war-crimes accountability, political legitimacy, religious mobilization, and due process. The judicial findings and criticism of the proceedings are distinct parts of this contested history.
highlight: Jamaat politician whose tribunal case became a central flashpoint of the 2013 Shahbag crisis.

shortAnswer: Delwar Hossain Sayeedi was a Jamaat politician convicted over 1971-related crimes whose case became central to the 2013 Shahbag conflict.

faq.answer: His tribunal conviction and sentence became a major trigger for the 2013 Shahbag mobilization and the counter-mobilization around war-crimes justice.
